content: Algor mortis, derived from the Latin words algor meaning coolness and mortis meaning of death, refers to the gradual reduction in body temperature following death. This cooling process typically continues in a steady manner until the body temperature equilibrates with the surrounding ambient temperature. However, external environmental factors can significantly influence the rate and extent of this cooling. The rectal temperature of a deceased individual can be measured to provide an approximate estimation of the time of death. On average, the body temperature decreases by about 5 degrees Fahrenheit per hour until it approaches the ambient temperature. This rate of cooling can be used to calculate the number of hours that have elapsed since death. As decomposition progresses, the internal body temperature may begin to rise again due to the metabolic activity of bacteria and other microorganisms involved in the decomposition process.
